turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Anil Deshmukh? Come through. I'll do the observations before the doctor sits.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister, it is me only. Sorry we are a bit late, the parking machine was not taking the coin. And then I was telling my wife we should not rush, because my back is already on my mind.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Let him sit, sister. He will give you the full novel otherwise.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. Arm out please. Blood pressure is one thirty-six over eighty-two, heart rate seventy-eight, oxygen ninety-eight.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): One thirty-six, ok ok. At the chemist last week the machine said something in that range, so I am a little relieved, these machines make me tense.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one second, this letter will not load. Right. I am with you now. Tell me what is happening.

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, actually the thing is, there is a mole on my back, left side, up near the shoulder blade. I myself cannot see it properly, even with two mirrors it becomes a whole confusion. So my wife has been the one checking it every few days.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The colour has changed. It was light brown, now one half is darker, almost blackish.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Say that again? The screen just flashed. Darker where?
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Left upper back. Half the mole is darker than it used to be. I saw it when he was changing his shirt.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, and I should give the background properly. We went to Goa for my cousin's wedding, that was six weeks back, and after that only she started saying the colour is not the same. Before that the mole was just sitting quietly for years, flat, I never bothered about it.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Six weeks. Ok. Any itching? Any pain?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No itching, doctor. No pain also. I kept checking with my finger, nothing like that, only the look has changed according to her.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It bled once. Last Sunday. Just a small smear on the vest, not pouring, after he dried his back hard with the towel.

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, only that one time. I got a proper fright, I washed it and pressed with cotton, and it stopped in about two minutes. From that Sunday till today, not a single drop, and I have been very gentle with the towel.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the cursor jumped. It bled once and then stopped? Which day?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Last Sunday, doctor. Only that one time. Nothing since.

[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ok. Shirt up, let me look. Hmm. It sits on the left scapula, there is asymmetry, the border is notched on the lower side, two colours, brown and a darker black-brown, roughly nine millimetres across, and there is no ulcer just now.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Nine millimetres, is that considered big, doctor? I should not google, I know, but my neighbour had something removed and he said size matters, and I could not sleep. My wife had to take my phone away.

[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): One moment, where has the cursor gone. Right. I would not call the size an emergency, but the colour mix and the notch are why I want skin specialist eyes on it. I am not putting a final name on it today.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He had very bad sunburns when he was young. Cricket all afternoon, no shirt, Nagpur heat.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually let me explain it properly, otherwise it sounds vague. From school till college, every summer the shoulders peeled, and at least three times I had blisters, my mother put curd on them, which was foolish. After about thirty-five I became careful with sleeves, but the last real burn was years ago, not nowadays.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Past burns, I have that. Any family skin cancer, or melanoma?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No doctor, nobody. My father had diabetes, my mother has blood pressure, but no skin cancer. I even phoned my elder brother last night and he also said no.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fine. And you, the pressure tablets, what are you actually taking? The list on my side looks old.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): On the chart it is amlodipin five mg, once a day.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No sister, that is the old dose only. They increased it, I am taking ten mg at night, the strip clearly says ten. The box is blue, near the fridge, my wife keeps all the strips in one place so I don't mix them.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The strip at home is ten mg. The file was never updated after that visit.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say the dose again, the screen jumped back. Five or ten?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten mg, doctor. Every night after food, I don't miss it. The chemist sometimes spells it amlodipin on the label, but it is amlodipine, same tablet.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ok. I will not guess between the chart and the strip, so the dose stays open till you bring it. Any allergy to a medicine, or a food?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all. No drug allergy and no food allergy. I have had penicillin for a tooth in the past, no rash, I remember because that tooth was a full drama by itself.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Any fever, any weight loss, night sweats?

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Weight is stable, I am careful with rice, and no night sweats. I do feel a bit tired in the evenings, but that is the shop, I stand from nine till eight, it is not some new sickness.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, breathlessness, cough?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of those. Breathing is fine. I climbed the stairs today without stopping, which I was quite happy about.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the tummy, any pain? Any burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No tummy pain, no burning. Appetite is normal, I had a full plate of idli this morning, same as always.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is outdoors a lot at the shop front. No smoking. Tea yes, alcohol no.

[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. My impression, and this is provisional only, is a changing mole with some worrying features. I cannot rule out a melanoma, and I also cannot tell you it is just a harmless naevus. Dermatology has to see it in person.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): The melanoma word is scary, I won't pretend otherwise, but I understand you are not confirming anything today. Kindly tell the plan straight, I will follow it, and my wife will also make sure I don't forget.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): I have booked the dermatology clinic for Tuesday morning, the week after next. That slot is fixed, it is not an if-needed thing. They will examine it with the dermatoscope.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Tuesday, week after next, morning. I will close the shop that day. Do I need to fast for them, or take anything special?

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not for the skin clinic. Separately, because it bled once and you are on a pressure tablet, the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, a full blood count and a kidney function. Come fasting, water only, take the night tablet as usual the evening before, and don't take Thursday's tablet until after the bloods.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday eight thirty, I will put him on the morning blood list. Fasting, yes.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning, fasting, tablet after the needle. I have noted it, sister, I will set an alarm so I don't eat by habit.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): And I will see you back here in two weeks, with those results, whether the skin appointment has happened or not.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If the blood report is not normal, then what?
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline we might do a ferritin, that would be a third test. I am not booking it now.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): And the mole itself, doctor, if it bleeds again before that Tuesday, what should we do? I keep imagining the vest stain, I am sorry, I overthink.

[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): If it does not settle, if it bleeds again or the dark part spreads, we might do a scan. I am not arranging any scan today. Otherwise keep it dry, don't scratch, shirt and a hat when you are at the shop front, and your wife can photograph it once a week in the same light, but nobody pokes it.

[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I will do all of that, no argument. My wife will take the photo, if I try to twist I will knock something, last time it was the lamp, whole story. Thank you, doctor, and thank you sister.
[SEG0053] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will bring the tablet strip next time, so the dose is not hanging in the air.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, bring the strip. Then we can correct the chart. Off you go, sorry I was half stuck on this screen.

spec.situation: Person with a mole on the back that partner says has changed in colour; bleeding once; sunburn history; doctor describes the mole by features and plans a dermatology referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Tiredness and relation to shop standing supported; severity 'mild' not stated.
bad.text: Evening tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, aggravating_factors=prolonged standing at the shop, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose is stated by the patient/family as 10 mg nightly after food; the recorded medication entry omits the dose.
No family history of melanoma was specifically asked and denied; only skin cancer is recorded.
No drug allergy and no food allergy were both specifically denied; the record only has a generic 'Allergies absent'.
Appetite normal was stated by the patient and not recorded.
Past history of repeated severe sunburns included shoulders peeling every summer in addition to at least three blistering episodes; the peeling detail is not recorded.
Dermatology plan included that they will examine the lesion with a dermatoscope; this investigation detail is not captured under procedures/investigations.
Follow-up was specified as 'with those results, whether the skin appointment has happened or not'; that condition is not recorded.

omissions.text: Current amlodipine dose is recorded incompletely: patient and family member said the current home strip is amlodipine 10 mg, taken every night after food, while the chart still showed the old 5 mg dose and the doctor left the dose unconfirmed until the strip is brought.
Patient said the mole had been flat and unchanged for years before the recent change after the Goa trip six weeks ago.
Family member reported the darker change affects about half the mole, becoming almost blackish.

Bleeding detail missing: the mole bled after he dried his back hard with a towel, left a small smear on the vest, stopped with pressure/cotton in about two minutes, and there has been no further bleeding since.
Past sun exposure history included severe sunburns in youth while playing cricket shirtless in Nagpur heat; after about age 35 he became more careful with sleeves and has not had a recent real burn.
Negative finding not recorded: no smoking was reported by family member, but also tea yes.
